transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-02
Time: 10:30 AM PST
Duration: 46 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (PacificMesh Partnerships), Aisha Rahman (PacificMesh Head of Solutions), Marco Silva (PacificMesh GPU Architect)

Summary: Intro / partner discovery between Redwood and PacificMesh. High-level business fit, integration patterns (marketplace, private deployment), security/compliance (SOC2, KMS), and next steps for pilot. Agreed to technical deep-dive and exchange of docs; discussed benchmark plan on PacificMesh H100 cluster.

Topics: partner intro; go-to-market / marketplace; technical integration options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC/on-prem); KMS/HSM and encryption; SOC2 and audit logs; sample benchmarks and quantization; pilot SOW and NDA.

Action items (quick): Jordan to send deck; Priya infra deep-dive; Marco share node configs; legal to exchange NDA.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. I'm Jordan, I lead partnerships at Redwood Inference - with me is Priya, she's our solutions engineer. How are you folks doing?
[00:08] Liam (PacificMesh): Good, thanks Jordan. Liam here, part of partner ops. Aisha and Marco are on as well. Appreciate the intro.
[00:13] Aisha (PacificMesh): Hi hi, morning all.
[00:15] Marco (PacificMesh): Morning. Quick note, my connection might be a little flaky, but should be fine.
[00:20] Jordan: Great, we'll keep it high level and then dive infra. Quick agenda: biz fit / GTM, technical integration options, security, and agree next steps. Sound good?
[00:29] Aisha: Yep, perfect.
[00:31] Jordan: Cool. High level - Redwood is an inference platform for running LLMs across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. We focus on predictable latency, cost controls, and tooling for rollouts, etc. We're looking to partner with infra/cloud vendors like PacificMesh to offer validated deployments and co-sell opportunities.
[00:45] Liam: Makes sense. From PacificMesh's side we're a cloud provider with focus on GPU compute for ML workloads. We operate bare-metal H100 clusters and have a marketplace for partner software. We're interested in making Redwood run smoothly on our infra and potentially joint go-to-market.
[00:58] Priya (Redwood SE): Thanks - from a technical perspective, typical partnership models we see are: 1) Marketplace listing where customers can spin up Redwood-hosted or Redwood-managed endpoints on your infra; 2) Certifying a private deployment pattern (VPC/VPN + KMS) for enterprise customers; 3) Pre-validated Dedicated images for customers to self-deploy on your hardware.
[01:20] Marco: On the hardware side we can expose bare-metal nodes or managed nodepools. We also have a private networking setup we call "mesh link" which is basically VPC peering plus a transit gateway. For keys we integrate with AWS KMS and we also have an HSM option.
[01:35] Jordan: Great - those capabilities line up well. Do you have existing partners who run inference runtimes on the platform?
[01:40] Liam: A couple, yes. We have a small list - some folks run custom serving stacks, others run marketplace images. Most requests we get are around compliance and data residency.
[01:49] Aisha: Exactly, a lot of our customers are telco and financial services so SOC2 and regional data residency are big.
[01:55] Priya: On the Redwood side we support SOC2 controls, audit logs, RBAC, SSO/SAML, and we can integrate with customer KMS or your HSM. For private deployments we usually provide a control plane that is customer-managed plus an agent set that runs in the customer's VPC.
[02:12] Marco: When you say agent, do you mean a full control plane container set or a lighter footprint? We prefer smaller surface area on nodes.
[02:18] Priya: Usually a lightweight control-plane component and runtime containers for the inference engine. The heavy lifting is on the GPU nodes - model weights, KV cache, batchers. We can tune the runtime for your node profiles; quantized kernels, attention optimizations, etc.
[02:33] Marco: Sounds good. Can you speak to network requirements? We have customers that require private peering and no public internet egress.
[02:40] Jordan: Yes - we support VPC-only control plane or private links. For fully air-gapped options we offer on-prem packages. We also have a compatibility matrix for port ranges and minimal outgoing endpoints, we'll share that.
[02:51] Liam: Perfect. On marketplace listing, what level of operational ownership would you want? Do you plan to manage the infra or would PMX customers take over?
[02:59] Jordan: We can support multiple models. For a marketplace offer we can provide an AMI/manifest so customers can self-deploy, or Redwood can run a managed offering on your infra with co-managed billing. There's also a middle ground - managed control plane with customer-owned compute.
[03:15] Aisha: For our enterprise accounts they'd likely want Redwood-managed software but PacificMesh-managed hardware, with an SLA.
[03:22] Priya: That is a common pattern. From an engineering perspective, we'd want a test/dev footprint to validate performance and then a pilot on a small cluster to collect telemetry and token-level cost numbers.
[03:33] Marco: For the pilot we can expose a 4-node H100 cluster. We're also curious about Redwood's batching behavior and KV cache to see how it behaves on multi-tenant hardware.
[03:43] Priya: Yeah - our runtime does continuous batching and respects per-tenant isolation for KV cache. We also support per-model quantization profiles. For reproducible benchmarks we'll want: model(s) to run, typical sequence lengths, concurrency, and target latency SLO.
[03:55] Jordan: We'll prepare a benchmark spreadsheet template and sample prompts, and propose a minimal test: 1) gpt-like 8k context LLM, 2) 256-token avg response, 3) burst concurrency patterns. That should show cost/latency tradeoffs and where Dedicated vs Hosted fits.
[04:10] Liam: Sounds good. Any red flags on supported frameworks? We primarily expose PyTorch and ONNX runtimes.
[04:16] Priya: We mostly run models in PyTorch/torchscript or ONNX; our runtime has optimized kernels for these. For custom builds we can provide container images.
[04:24] Marco: On security, SOC2 is fine but we need to know about audit logs and encryption at rest. Do you have per-tenant keying?
[04:31] Jordan: We support customer-managed KMS integration for encryption at rest and in-flight. Audit logs are available - token-level traces are optional and redacted for PII. We also expose RBAC and SSO/SAML. We'll share a SOC2 pack and network diagram.
[04:45] Aisha: Good. From GTM perspective, we'd want a co-branded marketplace tile and joint case study opportunities. What does Redwood typically require for marketing?
[04:54] Jordan: Normally a short partner one-pager, a technical validation (pilot), and a joint announcement once customers go live. We can do joint webinars and include you in our partner integrations page.
[05:05] Liam: Great. Any existing docs we should look at?
[05:08] Priya: We'll send our partner integration checklist, an ops runbook, and a minimal network port matrix. Also a sample helm chart for private deploys.
[05:17] Marco: For the pilot, access methods? Can you run against our internal private cluster or do you prefer to run on Redwood-managed instances?
[05:24] Priya: We can do either; preferred is to validate on your infra to surface integration issues, then run a controlled Redwood-managed run for metrics parity. For private clusters we'll need VPN/VPC peering and short-lived credentials.
[05:38] Aisha: About pricing - our customers ask about per-token costs and committed capacity. How does Redwood approach dedicated pricing?
[05:46] Jordan: We do usage-based pricing for hosted, and reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated with monthly/annual commits. We can share a pricing matrix for both managed and self-host models. For pilot we typically run a time-and-materials SOW.
[05:58] Liam: Okay. Any security checklist items that typically block deals?
[06:02] Priya: Common asks are SOC2, encryption/KMS, SSO, VPC-only control plane, audit logs retention. For some customers we need penetration test reports and a bug-bounty summary.
[06:12] Marco: We can provide compliance paperwork and a network diagram.
[06:15] Jordan: Perfect. We'll send our SOC2 summary and a short security FAQ.
[06:19] Priya: On the infra side, we'd like to schedule a 60 minute technical deep-dive with Marco and your infra team to go over node sizing, CUDA versions, driver compatibility, and container runtime. Can we pick a time next week?
[06:31] Marco: Yes, next week works. I'll send availabilities.
[06:34] Aisha: We'll also loop in bizops and legal for NDA.
[06:38] Jordan: Great. I'll also include a proposed pilot scope: 2-week validation, small scale (4 nodes), run our benchmark suite, and then a 30-day pilot extension if both sides are happy.
[06:50] Priya: One more technical note - we have a quantization compatibility matrix; for INT4/INT8 runs we might need to compile specific kernels. Marco, do you support custom kernel builds on your nodes?
[06:59] Marco: Yes, that's possible but we prefer to avoid frequent kernel changes across tenants; we can isolate via custom images per customer.
[07:07] Jordan: Sounds reasonable. We'll note that in the integration checklist.
[07:10] Liam: On co-selling, what partner motions does Redwood prefer - referral, reseller, or joint-managed accounts?
[07:16] Jordan: All of the above - typically we start with referrals and marketplace listing, then move to co-sell for larger enterprise deals. We'll discuss revenue share models after pilot results.
[07:26] Aisha: Okay. Anything else from Redwood?
[07:28] Priya: From SE side, logistics: we'll need SSH access or a test endpoint, container runtime details (docker vs containerd), driver versions, and sample TLS certs for the private link test.
[07:40] Marco: We'll prepare that.
[07:42] Jordan: Great. Let's recap. Next steps: Jordan sends partner deck, SOC2 summary, and pricing matrix; Priya schedules infra deep-dive and shares checklist; Marco shares node configs and test access; legal teams exchange NDA and draft pilot SOW. Agreed?
[07:57] All: Agreed.
[08:00] Jordan: Awesome - thanks everyone for the time. We'll follow up via email and create a shared folder for artifacts.
[08:07] Liam: Thanks Jordan, talk soon.
[08:09] Aisha: Thanks.
[08:10] Marco: Thanks, bye.

End of recording.
